newsitem.title: GREECE: WOMAN IN GREECE IS SISTER OF BERLIN BOMB SUSPECT.
newsitem.headline: WOMAN IN GREECE IS SISTER OF BERLIN BOMB SUSPECT.

text.p: A German woman detained in this northern port city is the sister of a key suspect in a 1986 disco bombing in West Berlin which killed three people and wounded 200, police sources said on Monday.
Two U.S. soldiers and a Turkish woman were killed in the attack on the Berlin club and scores of off-duty U.S. military personnel injured. It prompted a U.S. air strike against Libya.
Greek police arrested Andrea Hasler, 31, last Thursday in a hotel near Salonika at the request of German police. She has been jailed pending a hearing on a German extradition request.
Hasler is the sister of a woman identified as Verena C., 37, who was detained in Berlin last Thursday and accused of planting the bomb in the disco, the sources said.
They said German authorities had sent an extradition request to Greece and expected prompt action -- within less than a month -- under special European Union accords.
German prosecutors have given no details on what role they believe Hasler might have played in the bombing.

The extradition request will be a test for newly-elected Socialist Prime Minister Costas Simitis. His predecessor, late party founder Andreas Papandreou outraged his EU partners by refusing to extradite suspects in politically motivated crimes.
Government sources predicted Hasler's extradition would go through quickly. After passing the courts, it must be approved by Justice Minister Evangelos Yannopoulos.
Berlin prosecutors arrested Verena C. and her Palestinian ex-husband, Ali C., saying she was suspected of planting the deadly bomb at his request.

The United States blamed Libya for the attack on the "La Belle" disco and responded by bombing the Arab state, killing at least 15 people, including an adopted 15-month-old daughter of leader Muammar Gaddafi and wounding more than 100.
German prosecutors said they believed Verena C. had planted the bomb at the request of Ali C. and another suspect, Yasser Shraydi, who was extradited to Germany from Lebanon in May this year.

They believe the attack was orchestrated from the Libyan embassy in East Berlin. They have also issued arrest warrants for three former members of the Libyan embassy in East Berlin -- identified only by the surnames Elamin, Keshlaf and Al Abani -- and a Libyan secret service member named Rashed.
The prosecutors believe those suspects provided the explosives and helped organise the bombing but that they are now back in their homeland. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
